topic: Port and Harbour Safety: Risks and Controls Explained · Why port incidents occur at interfaces (1/4)

passage.text: There is an important pattern in serious port accidents. Investigations tend to find that the most dangerous incidents happen where two groups are working together on the same task. Each group may have a good safety system on its own. However, when the two systems meet, there is often no clear handover of responsibility. This appears to be where accidents are most likely to happen. The interface — the point where two groups connect — tends to contribute to failure more than any single group working alone.

source.title: Port and Harbour Safety: Risks and Controls Explained

taps.correct: This appears to be where accidents are most likely to happen.
wrong: Accidents definitely happen where there is no clear handover of responsibility.
taps.explain: Uses 'appears to' and 'likely' to show the writer is not completely certain.

taps.prompt: What is the main idea of the text?
taps.correct: Serious port accidents happen most often where responsibility is unclear between different groups.
wrong: Groups working alone always have dangerous safety systems.
Port accidents are caused by groups that refuse to work together.
taps.explain: The text focuses on unclear responsibility at the interface, not on solo work or refusal to cooperate.
